sources.citation: Miklukho-Maklai, N. N. 2020 [1st ed. of this collected-works edition 1993; texts of 1873-1877]. Sobranie sochinenii v shesti tomakh. 2-e izd., ispr. i dop. Tom 3: Stat'i i materialy po antropologii i etnografii narodov Okeanii (otv. red. D. D. Tumarkin, N. N. Miklukho-Maklai ml.). Sankt-Peterburg. 465 pp. Therein: 'Papuasskie dialekty Berega Maklaia na Novoi Gvinee' (pp. 143-156; comparative table col. 5 Englam-Mana), 'Chislitel'nye v dialektakh Berega Maklaia' (p. 157), 'Spisok nekotorykh slov i obraztsov rechi, sobrannykh na Beregu Maklaia v 1876-1877 gg.' (pp. 158-160), commentary pp. 399-403.
sources.note: No phonology content for Englam-Mana: three wordlists (1873 comparative list c. 62 items + numerals, col. 5 'Энглам-Мана (горная деревня)', e.g. улен 'sun', саем 'moon', генагулум 'woman', олам 'ear'/'one'; numerals table 'Энглам': alalam, ari, kini, wali, andosam, kilmussi; 1876-77 list of 76 items, e.g. bunangar 'sky', tatuo 'wind', inakum 'woman') printed in Cyrillic/Latin WITHOUT stress marks. Accents appear only on the Bongu personal names (p. 153) and editorial note 6* states 'В рукописи далее ударения отсутствуют' ('in the manuscript, accents are absent from here on'). sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Rai Coast languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-30. Canberra: ANU. xvi+196 pp. doi 10.15144/PL-D30
sources.note: Nothing. Yangulam = B24 (Nuru Family). Introduction sec. 7 (pp. vii-viii) describes a 'semiphonemic' transcription and lists fluctuating sounds per language; no mention of stress, accent or tone (note 3, p. 172, says only that Dumpu-Watiwa is tonal). B24 wordlist forms are printed without stress marks (checked page scan, printed p. 3: ilaŋgum, monaguru).

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1975a. The Madang-Adelbert Range Sub-Phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study 1 (PL C-38), 569-612. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing. B24 Yangulam, 180 speakers, member of the Nuru Family (sec. 2.8.2.2.1.1.5, p. 581); typological/pronoun/lexical tables only.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1975b. The languages of the Madang District, Papua New Guinea. PL B-41. Canberra: ANU. doi 10.15144/PL-B41
sources.note: Nothing (gazetteer). B24 Yangulam 180: villages Sekwanam 100, Yangulam 80; identifies Miklucho-Maclay's 'Englam-Mana, Sambul, Seguana-Mana' and Englam/Jenglam/Tangulam/Yanglam of older sources with B24 Yangulam.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. PL C-19. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing on Yangulam: sec. 2.4.13 'Jenglam or Englam JEN(?)' is known only from Maclay's wordlist in Gabelentz-Meyer (1883:500-2). The p. 7 survey-wide disclaimer ('The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet') applies to Z'graggen's own lists, which did not yet include Yangulam.

sources.citation: Claassen, O. R. & K. A. McElhanon. 1970. Languages of the Finisterre Range - New Guinea. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 11 (PL A-23), 45-78.
sources.note: Nothing on Yangulam; the Nuru-family area was not surveyed. Rai Coast phonology notes (sec. 6.1) cover Yaganon, Suroi ('stress is contrastive, but only on a limited number of words', p. 66) and Evapia only.

sources.note: Nothing. 'Englam. - Mountain village north-east of Sungumana' listed in the 'Bongu or Astrolabe Group' (p. 321); comparative grammatical notes drawn from Maclay/Hanke; no prosody.
